title: Cotangent coordinates of a Tate algebra at a separable closed point
statement:
Let $F$ be a field complete for a nontrivial real-valued nonarchimedean absolute value, and let $r\geq0$. Let $T=F\langle x_1,\ldots,x_rangle$ be the ring of series $\sum_{
u\in\mathbf N^r}a_
u x^
u$ such that, for every $\epsilon>0$, only finitely many coefficients satisfy $|a_
u|\geq\epsilon$, with coefficientwise addition and Cauchy multiplication. Let $\mathfrak n$ be a maximal proper ideal of $T$ and put $\kappa=T/\mathfrak n$. Suppose $\kappa/F$ is finite separable, meaning finite-dimensional over $F$ with every element having a minimal polynomial with distinct roots. Set $R=T_{\mathfrak n}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] and $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak nR$. Then $R$ is a regular Noetherian local ring [def-weil-regular-scheme], with maximal ideal $\mathfrak p$ and residue map $ho:R	o\kappa$ given by $h/u\mapsto ar h/ ar u$. The following rule is a well-defined $\kappa$-linear isomorphism:
$$	heta:\mathfrak p/\mathfrak p^2\xrightarrow{\sim}\kappa^{\oplus r},\qquad [h/u]\longmapsto\left( rac{\overline{\partial h/\partial x_i}}{ ar u}ight)_{i=1}^r\quad(h\in\mathfrak n,\ u
otin\mathfrak n).$$
The derivatives are termwise derivatives of restricted series. The scalar structure on $\mathfrak p/\mathfrak p^2$ is induced by $R/\mathfrak p=\kappa$. For $r=0$, one has $T=R=\kappa=F$, $\mathfrak n=\mathfrak p=0$, and the displayed isomorphism is between zero spaces.

source.place: Theorem 1.1.5(1), PDF p.4, regularity of Tate algebras; separable-point first-order refinement formulated by the agent using Conrad, Irreducible components of rigid spaces, https://www.numdam.org/article/AIF_1999__49_2_473_0.pdf, section 1.1 printed p.477 and proof of Lemma 3.3.1 printed p.510. Read online 2026-10-24; archival copies WANTED.

proof.text: By [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], $R$ is local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak nR$. Every element of $\mathfrak p$ has a representative $h/u$ with $h\in\mathfrak n$ and $u\notin\mathfrak n$: put a finite sum of ideal fractions over a common denominator. The formula $\rho(h/u)=\bar h/\bar u$ respects the fraction relation, since every denominator and every clearing factor outside $\mathfrak n$ has nonzero image in the field $\kappa$. It is surjective (lift each element of $\kappa$ to $T$) and its kernel is exactly $\mathfrak p$. Thus $R/\mathfrak p=\kappa$.

source.place: Theorem 1.1.5(1), PDF p.4; agent first-order refinement using polynomial comparison and Stacks Tags 00OP, 07NY, 07NV, 00KU.

proof.text: Put $P=F[x_1,\ldots,x_r]$. Apply [lem-trf-affinoid-polynomial-closed-point-comparison] with $J=0$, $C=T$ and the given maximal ideal $\mathfrak n$. It says that $T$ is Noetherian, that $\mathfrak m=\mathfrak n\cap P$ is maximal, and that the induced local map $A=P_{\mathfrak m}\to R$ gives a ring isomorphism $\widehat A\simeq\widehat R$. By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian], $R$ is Noetherian. By [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-field-regular-ring], $A$ is Noetherian regular local; [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-maximal-localization-dimension] gives $\dim A=r$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-completion-regular-local] to $A$ and then $R$: the isomorphism of their completed local rings proves $R$ regular. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-completion-dimension] to both rings to obtain $\dim R=\dim\widehat R=\dim\widehat A=\dim A=r$. All completion results here have their required Noetherian local hypotheses.

source.place: Theorem 1.1.5(1), PDF p.4; agent first-order refinement using polynomial comparison and Stacks Tags 00OP, 07NY, 07NV, 00KU.

proof.text:
For each $i$, termwise differentiation gives an $F$-linear derivation $d_i:T	o T$. Indeed, $|n\cdot1_F|\leq1$ for every natural number $n$, by the strong triangle inequality, so the coefficient $(
u_i+1)a_{
u+e_i}$ of $d_i h$ still tends to zero. The coefficient of a fixed monomial in a product is a finite Cauchy sum; differentiating it and using $\alpha_i+ eta_i=
u_i$ proves the Leibniz rule coefficient by coefficient. Compose with $T	o\kappa$ and extend to fractions by $$D_i(h/u)= rac{ ar u\,\overline{d_i h}- ar h\,\overline{d_i u}}{ ar u^2}.$$ To check independence, differentiate a clearing relation $s(hu'-h'u)=0$ with $s
otin\mathfrak n$ and reduce modulo $\mathfrak n$. The undifferentiated relation kills the term involving $d_i s$, and cancellation of $ ar s$ gives equality of the two displayed values. The same product and sum rules show that $D_i$ is an $F$-derivation to the $R$-module $\kappa$ with scalar map $ho$.

source.place: Theorem 1.1.5(1), PDF p.4; agent first-order refinement using polynomial comparison and Stacks Tags 00OP, 07NY, 07NV, 00KU.

proof.text: For $a,b\in\mathfrak p$ the Leibniz rule gives $D_i(ab)=\rho(a)D_i(b)+\rho(b)D_i(a)=0$. Thus $D=(D_i)_i$ kills $\mathfrak p^2$. For $t\in R$, $a\in\mathfrak p$, it gives $D(ta)=\rho(t)D(a)$, so the induced map $\theta:\mathfrak p/\mathfrak p^2\to\kappa^{\oplus r}$ is $\kappa$-linear. If $a=h/u$ with $h\in\mathfrak n$, the term involving $\bar h$ vanishes in step 3, giving exactly the formula in the statement. This proves both its well-definedness and the asserted scalar convention.

source.place: Theorem 1.1.5(1), PDF p.4; agent first-order refinement using polynomial comparison and Stacks Tags 00OP, 07NY, 07NV, 00KU.

proof.text: Write $a_i=\bar x_i\in\kappa$, and let $f_i(Z)\in F[Z]$ be its monic minimal polynomial. Finite separability makes $f_i'(a_i)\ne0$: in a splitting field the derivative at a root is the product of its differences from all other roots, each nonzero. Now $h_i=f_i(x_i)\in\mathfrak n$, and coefficient differentiation gives $\theta([h_i/1])=f_i'(a_i)e_i$, where $e_i$ is the $i$th coordinate vector. Multiplying this class by $f_i'(a_i)^{-1}\in\kappa$ gives a preimage of $e_i$. Therefore $\theta$ is surjective; this uses only polynomials inside $T$, not a choice of coefficient field in $R$.

source.place: Theorem 1.1.5(1), PDF p.4; agent first-order refinement using polynomial comparison and Stacks Tags 00OP, 07NY, 07NV, 00KU.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-cotangent-dimension] to the Noetherian regular local ring $R$ obtained in step 2. It gives $\dim_\kappa(\mathfrak p/\mathfrak p^2)=\dim R=r$. A surjective map between these two vector spaces of dimension $r$ has zero kernel: lift the $r$ standard basis vectors as in step 5; they are linearly independent because their images are, hence form a basis of the source, and $\theta$ sends that basis to the standard basis. Thus $\theta$ is an isomorphism. When $r=0$, a restricted series is just its constant coefficient, so $T=F$, its only maximal proper ideal is zero, $R=\kappa=F$ and $\mathfrak p=0$. This verifies the degenerate clause as well.
